title: Embedded Detail Documents
summary: Durable source, payload, URL, manifest, lifecycle, and runtime contract for report-hosted detail documents outside the main index.
content_html:
Embedded Detail Documents

Embedded detail documents let a normal indexed Docs Viewer document host a large set of Docs Viewer-owned detail documents without adding every detail document to the main index tree or global docs search.

The pattern is useful when the discovery surface should be a report or list inside a parent document rather than the Docs Viewer sidebar. The parent document stays selected, the sidebar stays anchored to that parent, and detail documents are loaded into a report-owned region on demand.

Detail documents are still first-class Docs Viewer source docs. They use the normal Markdown, front matter, media-token, doc-link, rendering, by-id payload, and publish pipeline. The embedded-detail model changes discovery and presentation; it does not create a weaker detail-document format.

Source Layout

A sub-scope is a detail-document grouping below a normal Docs Viewer scope. It is not a full navigable scope and must not appear in the scope selector.

source: docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/source/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/documents/
local published: docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/
public projection: site/assets/data/docs/scopes/<scope>/<sub-scope>/

The parent scope owns the indexed report document. The sub-scope owns the detail payloads and list manifests that the parent report loads.

Main-scope builds explicitly ignore configured sub-scope source directories for:

  • index-tree.json
  • recent.json
  • global docs search

Sub-scope builds write by-ID payloads, a minimal public-safe manifest, and a richer local Manage manifest.

Parent Report

A normal indexed source document opts into the generic sub-scope report with one body block:

:::report
id: docs_subscope
access: public
sub_scope: tags
:::

Attributes:

  • id: selects the docs_subscope report module
  • sub_scope: names the configured sub-scope that the report may load
  • access: follows the normal report access model; use public only when the report is promoted and allowlisted for public routes

The sub-scope is configured by the parent document payload, not by a URL query parameter. This prevents the generic report from becoming an arbitrary sub-scope loader.

Authored content before or after the block belongs to the parent document and renders normally; the generated report mounts at the block's exact position.

URL State

The active Docs Viewer document remains the indexed parent/report document. The standard report-owned detail parameter is subdoc.

/docs/?scope=<scope>&doc=<parent_doc_id>
/docs/?scope=<scope>&doc=<parent_doc_id>&subdoc=<detail_doc_id>

For a public route:

/analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639
/analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260624-204534-e3de0b

In the detail URL:

  • doc=d-20260624-213316-478639 is still the selected Docs Viewer document
  • subdoc=d-20260624-204534-e3de0b is report-owned state
  • refresh reloads the parent report and opens the embedded detail document
  • browser Back/Forward moves between report list/detail states without selecting the detail document in the sidebar

The shared route helpers preserve subdoc only when the route still points at the indexed parent document. Normal document navigation clears report-owned detail state.

Runtime Behavior

The docs_subscope report:

  • reads report.sub_scope from the selected parent document payload
  • validates the configured sub-scope against the current scope's browser-facing config
  • loads the route-configured public or Manage list manifest
  • applies default title search and title-ascending list order
  • resolves only an access-registered collection customisation
  • reads subdoc from the current URL
  • derives detail payload URLs from the current scope, configured sub-scope, and selected detail id
  • renders list state when subdoc is absent
  • renders detail state only when subdoc is listed and the loaded payload repeats the requested doc_id
  • renders a contained report error when subdoc is unknown or a detail payload fails to load
  • updates only report-owned URL state when rows or the report back control are used
  • never updates Docs Viewer selected-document state to the sub-scope detail document

The report owns:

  • selected detail id
  • embedded detail payload loading
  • detail-region rendering
  • subdoc URL state

Docs Viewer owns:

  • active scope
  • active parent/report document
  • sidebar tree selection
  • parent document payload rendering
  • report mounting hook

Title search remains default report state. Optional collection filters are supplied through registered customisations; neither changes the selected Docs Viewer document.

List And Detail States

List state shows the sub-scope list from the configured manifest and lets the user select a row. It keeps the complete manifest for detail validation while deriving visible rows from a case-insensitive title prefix. Manage can switch between title ascending and last_updated descending. Additional constraints come only from the selected registered customisation.

In Manage mode, the standard contribution adds status and, for a publish-capable collection, publishability treatment, New, collection-local checkbox selection, Actions, Prepare Package, Copy Link, and validated-detail Delete. An optional registered customisation is composed after it. Selection receives the visible eligible projection so Select all excludes filtered-out rows but includes both publishable and non-publishable rows. Checkbox interaction does not navigate; only checked IDs target a selection action, filtering does not silently remove existing checked IDs, and unmount or collection change clears that owner.

Detail state:

  • hides the list and list header completely
  • leaves Back plus any validated-detail contribution controls
  • renders the selected detail document inside the report surface
  • provides a Back control that clears subdoc and restores the mounted filter state

The embedded detail body reuses normal Docs Viewer rendered-document styling. Report-specific detail CSS provides only containment, spacing, and the report toolbar/divider. It must not redefine document typography, table, image, or link styling.

Representative structure:

<section class="docsReportDetail" aria-label="ordered">
  <div class="docsReportDetail__header">
    <button type="button" aria-label="Back to all tags">←</button>
  </div>
  <article class="docsReportDetail__body docsViewer__content content"></article>
</section>

The detail body receives the selected by-id payload's content_html. The detail wrapper should not be a card, panel, or secondary document frame.

Manifest Contract

Each sub-scope builds a minimal public-safe manifest. The public manifest is an existence, ordering, and list-label contract, not an index tree. A sibling Manage manifest retains private status, false-only publishability for a publish-capable collection, last_updated, and any namespaced customisation data as described in Sub-Scope Public And Manage Manifests.

{
  "docs": [
    {"doc_id": "d-20260624-204534-0d6ae2", "title": "bird"},
    {"doc_id": "d-20260624-204534-ecfc12", "title": "nerve"}
  ]
}

Field requirements:

  • docs: ordered records containing the stable detail doc_id and its human title

The title is included because opaque IDs cannot provide a useful list label. Body content and full document metadata remain in the selected by-id payload.

The report derives all other runtime information:

  • parent scope from the active Docs Viewer scope
  • sub-scope from report.sub_scope
  • selected detail id from subdoc
  • by-id payload URL from browser-facing sub-scope config
  • list labels from explicit report metadata sources

Sub-scope detail documents may still carry normal Docs Viewer metadata such as parent_id. The generic docs_subscope report does not treat that metadata as list hierarchy. Nested detail navigation or grouping should be a later report-specific extension that reads explicit list metadata.

By-Id Payload Contract

Sub-scope detail documents publish the same by-id JSON shape as normal Docs Viewer documents. The payload keeps normal rendered content and metadata, including:

  • doc_id
  • title
  • last_updated
  • content_html
  • front matter-derived fields exposed by the normal by-id payload contract

The generic report renders content_html, and keeps by-id metadata available for labels, diagnostics, and future promotion workflows.

Keeping the full by-id shape preserves the option to promote a detail document into an indexed document later without changing its source Markdown model.

Detail Identity

Sub-scope detail ids only need to be unique within their owning <scope>/<sub-scope>. They do not need to be unique across the whole parent scope.

Runtime detail identity is resolved from:

<scope> + <parent_report_doc_id> + <subdoc>

Cross-report references, logs, and caches should preserve enough context to resolve through the parent report config, or use a composite identity such as:

<scope>/<sub-scope>/<doc_id>

Raw detail doc_id values should not be treated as globally unique.

Link Resolution

Detail documents may contain normal same-sub-scope Markdown links. When a sub-scope has exactly one matching indexed parent report document, the sub-scope builder rewrites same-sub-scope links to the embedded report-detail URL.

Example:

source detail link: related.md
rendered href: /docs/?scope=<scope>&doc=<parent_doc_id>&subdoc=<detail_doc_id>

If the builder cannot identify a unique parent docs_subscope report for the sub-scope, it falls back to the normal Docs Viewer doc URL and records a warning for ambiguous parent report matches.

Sub-Scope Config

Sub-scopes are declared inside the parent scope config record. They are not top-level scopes.

Abbreviated sub-scope record:

{
  "sub_scope": "tags",
  "title": "Tags",
  "source": {
    "location": { "provider": "repository", "path": "docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/source/sub-scopes/tags" },
    "documents_path": "documents",
    "build_media": {},
    "sub_scopes_path": "sub-scopes"
  },
  "published": {
    "documents": { "location": { "provider": "repository", "path": "docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/published/documents/sub-scopes/tags" } },
    "search": { "location": { "provider": "repository", "path": "docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/published/search/sub-scopes/tags/index.json" } },
    "media": {}
  },
  "public_projection": {
    "documents": { "location": { "provider": "repository", "path": "site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/tags" } },
    "search": null
  }
}

Browser-facing config projects each sub-scope with enough safe data for the report. Manage config points to the local published child projection:

{
  "sub_scope": "tags",
  "title": "Tags",
  "manifest_url": "/docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/published/documents/sub-scopes/tags/manage-manifest.json",
  "by_id_url_base": "/docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/published/documents/sub-scopes/tags/by-id",
  "sub_scope_customisation": {"id": "analysis_tags"}
}

Public config points to the public projection:

{
  "sub_scope": "tags",
  "title": "Concepts",
  "manifest_url": "/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/tags/manifest.json",
  "by_id_url_base": "/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/tags/by-id"
}

Public reports must read only browser-safe generated or published projections. They must not read source Markdown files directly.

The local report loads manage-manifest.json through the same shared manifest loader. That generated projection contains every configured child, including non-publishable records, plus the standard Manage fields and any registered customisation namespace. It is excluded from publication.

Build And Publish

build_docs.py remains the orchestration entrypoint. Sub-scope builds use:

./docs-viewer/build/build_docs.py --scope studio --sub-scope tags --write

The sub-scope build path reuses the normal Docs Viewer pipeline:

  • source parsing
  • front matter normalization
  • Markdown and raw HTML rendering
  • media token resolution
  • doc-link rewriting
  • deterministic JSON writing

The builder writes local published JSON:

docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/by-id/<doc_id>.json
docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/manifest.json
docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/manage-manifest.json

For public scopes, the existing parent-scope Publish action copies configured sub-scope manifests and by-id payloads to:

site/assets/data/docs/scopes/<scope>/<sub-scope>/by-id/<doc_id>.json
site/assets/data/docs/scopes/<scope>/<sub-scope>/manifest.json

The builder does not write public snapshots directly. Publishing remains part of the existing parent-scope publish preview/apply flow.

The Docs Live Rebuild Watcher treats configured sub-scope source changes as sub-scope builds. It does not run parent-scope docs or search rebuilds for sub-scope-only source changes.

Lifecycle

Sub-scopes are managed alongside normal Docs Viewer scope management with dedicated lifecycle actions:

  • New sub-scope
  • Delete sub-scope

These actions operate within the selected parent scope. They do not create public routes, add the sub-scope to the main scope selector, or make sub-scope documents directly selectable in the main sidebar.

New sub-scope asks for the sub-scope id and title only. Sub-scopes do not have a default document concept.

Delete sub-scope uses preview and confirmation because it can remove source docs, local published payloads, and public-projection payloads.

Constraints

  • A sub-scope is not a full scope in the route model or scope selector.
  • Main scope builders must exclude configured sub-scope source directories from index, recent, and search payloads.
  • Sub-scope builders must keep using the normal Docs Viewer rendering and by-id payload pipeline.
  • Published sub-scopes must include a minimal public-safe manifest so the report can validate, order, and label detail ids without loading a tree, search index, or every document payload. Manage reads the sibling local manifest.
  • subdoc is reserved for docs_subscope detail state.
  • Public sub-scope publishing remains part of the parent-scope Publish action.
  • Public manifests should not repeat scope, sub-scope, payload URLs, or document bodies. Detail titles are the one list-label field they own.

Public And Manage Behavior

Public behavior:

  • parent/report doc appears in the public index when publishable
  • the list presents its configured public title and filters locally by title prefix without group controls
  • detail payloads are loadable through the report and report-owned links
  • global docs search does not include sub-scope detail docs by default
  • published payloads include the parent report, configured sub-scope manifests, and required detail by-id payloads

Manage behavior:

  • parent/report doc behaves like any report-backed Docs Viewer document
  • the parent remains selected in the index while subdoc stays report-owned URL state
  • list rows come from the complete private inventory and can show Status plus, for a publish-capable collection, the Excluded from next Publish marker
  • title-prefix and optional document-group controls derive a visible eligible projection without changing the complete manifest
  • the collection has an independent checkbox owner with compact 🔧 Actions, Select all, Clear, and Done controls
  • Prepare Package receives exact checked child IDs plus { scope, sub_scope }, treats the collection as flat, and records that identity in result, operation logs, metadata, and external context
  • every prepared child package is export-only and excluded from actionable Returned Packages, Docs Review, and Docs Import
  • Parent Source always supplies { scope, doc_id } for the indexed parent, even while a detail is displayed
  • Subdoc Source and subdoc Edit metadata are enabled only for a listed, successfully loaded detail whose payload identity matches the requested id
  • subdoc workflows supply { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }; missing, unlisted, failed, mismatched, or path-escaping targets do not fall back to the parent
  • source and metadata success refresh the targeted detail and inventory, then remount the same parent report route
  • sub-scope detail documents remain absent from the parent index, Recent, and global search

Public behavior continues to use only the publishable { doc_id, title } manifest and compact by-ID payloads. It receives no management inventory, Status/publishability markers, source controls, or metadata actions.
